summary: This component fetches and displays comments from Bluesky (a social media platform) for a blog post. It converts Bluesky's post data into readable React components, handling text with links, embedded images, and nested reply threads with proper indentation based on reply depth.

explanations.13: Bluesky stores text positions as byte offsets (counting individual bytes in UTF-8 encoding) rather than character positions, which matters for emojis and accented letters that take multiple bytes.
explanations.20: TextEncoder converts the post text into raw bytes so we can slice it using Bluesky's byte-offset indices, which wouldn't work correctly with regular string slicing.
explanations.27: We loop through each 'facet' (a marked-up piece of text like a link) and collect the plain text before it, the facet itself (rendered as a link if applicable), then continue from where that facet ended.
explanations.34: We search through the facet's features to find if this particular piece of text is marked as a link; if not, it's rendered as plain text.
explanations.69: Instead of checking the `$type` field (which can be any string for unknown embed types), we check if the 'external' property exists to safely narrow the type to an external link embed.
explanations.87: Similar type-narrowing: we check for the presence of an 'images' property to identify image embeds and render them as a gallery.
explanations.113: We extract the last part of the post's URI (a unique identifier) by splitting on slashes — this becomes the post ID needed to build shareable URLs.
explanations.127: The padding increases with reply depth so nested replies indent further: each level adds 1.5rem (depth starts at 0, so top-level replies have 1.5rem padding).
explanations.203: We construct Bluesky's standard post URI format using the account handle and record key from the blog's metadata.
explanations.205: We use encodeURIComponent to safely encode the URI in the query string, protecting special characters like colons and slashes.
explanations.213: This recursive function walks through the reply tree, flattening it into a single array while recording each reply's depth level so we can render indentation.
explanations.225: Once we've successfully fetched and flattened the comments, we update React state to trigger a re-render with the actual comments displayed.
explanations.237: Until the fetch completes, `comments` stays null; we show a loading message in this intermediate state.
